body.x: Awesome Lab (CEO Martin Kim) won the Gadgety Award, which each year selects the most innovative products at CES through the votes of global IT media and experts.

The Gadgety Award operates independently from the CES Innovation Awards presented by CTA, the organizer of CES. It is hosted by an independent body composed of editors-in-chief and founders from four technology-focused media outlets—Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Isa Does Tech, and Phandroid—and emphasizes real-world usability and impact in the global market. The awards cover a wide range of tech, including smart home devices, audio equipment, AI innovations, and gaming gear.

Awesome Lab is a startup that has developed electric hot water and heating solutions based on water electrolysis–powered ionized heating technology. Since first developing the technology in 2022, the company has secured domestic and international patents and certifications.
At CES 2026, Awesome Lab introduced its hot water and heating solution “Thermoflux” and achieved the milestone of winning the Gadgety Award.

Thermoflux operates by applying ionization reactions generated during the electrical activation of water, producing heat directly from the water itself without the need for separate heaters or combustion processes.

At CES 2026 in the United States, Thermoflux demonstrated its applicability beyond hot-water supply and heating, showing potential for use across a wide range of industrial environments that require continuous heat supply. Moreover, as an electrically driven system without combustion, it drew attention as an effective alternative to conventional hot water and heating systems amid tightening gas boiler regulations and global decarbonization policies.

An Awesome Lab official said, “At CES 2026, we were able to confirm strong global market interest in our next-generation hot water and heating solution. Global visitors and buyers highly evaluated objective data demonstrating improved heating responsiveness, carbon reduction, and tangible performance, as well as comparisons with existing boiler systems.”

The official added, “Through the networks formed at CES, our goal is to concretely develop partnerships for overseas pilot projects and commercialization and to open new global sales channels. Having already accumulated meaningful data and references through PoC projects conducted in Japan, the United States, and Mongolia, we positively assess the potential to attract new customers and partners.”

The Gadgety Awards is a global technology awards program that honors the most innovative and practical products showcased at major IT exhibitions such as CES, MWC, and IFA. It recognizes, honors, and celebrates the most innovative consumer electronics and mobile technology at major trade shows such as CES and ShowStoppers. Judged by expert tech editors, the awards spotlight products with exceptional design, functionality, and market impact. At CES 2026, winners included companies like Samsung and Anker Innovations, as well as various AI-powered, robotic, health-focused, and sustainable gadgets.
